ref: Archival Capture: Overhead scanning at 300/400 dpi for text and 600 dpi for
manuscripts/photos, in 24-bit colour. [1]
OCR & AV Processing: OpenCV + Tesseract for print; FFmpeg → Whisper-small
for timestamped transcripts. [2]
Source Records: TIFF/LZW masters [1], SHA-256 checksums [3] and page/time
chunks linked to source versions.
Metadata & Maps: Dublin Core tags and access-rights metadata [4], with curator-
reviewed entity/date relationships.
Hybrid Ranking: Multilingual E5-small: 384-dimension vectors [5] + PostgreSQL
text search; fuse ranks using RRF. [6]
RAG Pipeline: Filter access; retrieve evidence → generate context-based
answers [7] → resolve citation IDs.
Avatar Transport: WebRTC media + authenticated streaming API and LAM
(Large Avatar Model)[8]; connect conversations to archive retrieval.
Update Pipeline: Source-version changes flag derivatives; review, publish
manifests and refresh connected devices.
Prototype Host: Reuse a laptop/mini PC; target 4 cores, 16 GB RAM, 256 GB SSD.
Touch Kiosk: 32” FHD capacitive screen [9], browser PC, mic and headphones.
Smart Display: 43” 4K HDMI panel [9] with a player; reuse compatible screens.
Local Network: Connect the host, kiosks, displays and staff PCs over 1 GbE.
Backup & Power: Use a UPS, independent backups and regular restore checks.
Integration: Reuse compatible hosts; DAIC research PCs [10] enable access.
new: Rule Sources: Link each approval to the official act and service rule [1,2]
with sources, jurisdictions and validity.
Rule Encoding: OPA / Rego checks typed facts; returns reasons or warnings
for unresolved requirements. [9]
Case Records: Store profiles, source clauses, versions and saved evidence
links beside every case snapshot.
Dependency Plan: Use NetworkX to order tasks and check prerequisites [10], with
reviewed departmental dependencies.
Document Intake: pypdf extracts; Tesseract transcribes scanned documents [11]
then ask staff to check parsed fields.
Case Workflow: Track submission, officer queries and inspection booking
with the decision made by officers.
Service Clocks: Track receipt, query and response events per service
with service-specific calendars and applicable pause conditions. [2]
Change Processing: Operational changes flag requirements; review, compare
documents and retain previous snapshots.
Portal UI: React and TypeScript give each role a view of the same shared case.
API Service: FastAPI validates each case and records its state with events.
Rule Engine: OPA checks facts and NetworkX labels each task ready or blocked.
Batch Jobs: Queue OCR and alerts, then retry safe calls to each department.
Data Store: Log case records in PostgreSQL and files with access controls.
Integration: API adapters sync official status; demo calls stay simulated.

ref: MVP Hardware: Reuse a laptop, one touch
device and a second display.

reviewed pages and 3 AV items.
Workload Control: Batch OCR and transcription
before interactive sessions.
Integration Checks: Test touch, audio, display
playback and device sync.
Equipment Reuse: Assess institutional PCs and
screens before new purchases.
AI Running Cost: Budget paid avatar usage [8]
and enforce session limits.
Content Reuse: Store approved translations and
narration for local replay.
Staff Ownership: Curators approve content; IT
manages devices and backups.
new: Test Units: Model two factories and one
change in a working profile.
Pilot Checks: Twenty profiles plus twelve
files and ten case flow tests.
Workload Control: Schedule OCR and extraction
before departmental reviews.
Adapter Checks: Log events, receipt, deadlines
and failed API responses.
Portal Fit: Connect authorised interfaces and
imports with tracked sources.
AI Usage Costs: Cap optional model usage fees
and retain source excerpts.
Evidence Reuse: Check permissions and validity
before each new submission.
Policy Ownership: Reviewers approve rules; IT
manages systems and backups.

ref: Expected impact: Broader access to Ambedkar’s legacy, with evidence people can inspect and institutions can preserve.
Visitors: Ask the avatar follow-up questions and explore original sources.
Students & Educators: Understand constitutional ideas through timelines and
debates.
Researchers: Save cited excerpts and AV timestamps in one research
collection.
Curators: Review corrections and republish affected stories across exhibits.
Accessible Learning: Multilingual text, captions and narration widen access.
Constitutional Awareness: Link rights and equality to Ambedkar’s original works.
Heritage Conservation: Digital access copies reduce routine handling of originals.
Resource Efficiency: Reuse compatible equipment and approved media across
displays.
new: Expected impact: Fewer filing errors and clear next actions, with recorded decisions across the industrial lifecycle.
Applicants: See required approvals and understand the next action clearly.
Industrial Units: Identify renewal requirements and review planned business
changes.
Officers: Review evidence changes and queries within one full case
chronology.
Inspectors: Coordinate selected visits and review assigned case information.
Submission Readiness: Catch omissions upfront and reuse authorised evidence.
Visible Accountability: Separate applicant response time from the officer clock.
Multilingual Guidance: Explain requirements with Marathi and English source links.
Scheme Discovery: Assess eligibility criteria and documents with official
services.
